note: The single source of truth for what changed on Operations Academia. Read by the About page's 'What's new' list, by the live preview inside the e-mail alerts form, and by the alerts mailer, which sends every entry dated inside a subscriber's window. To announce something, add an entry dated ~today; an entry dated in the past reaches nobody, so seeding history is safe.

updates.title: Posting a job: the university, school and department boxes now follow each other
updates.summary: The three name boxes on the job form are connected. Choose your university and the school box offers that university’s schools; choose one of those and the department box offers that school’s departments — so a posting takes a few seconds and lands under the names everybody else uses. They reach further than the postings, too: every university, school and department in the site’s own Universities directory is offered, so a university posting here for the first time gets the same help, and choosing a department the site has only ever seen in one school fills that school in above it. Nothing is closed off — typing searches every name on the site, and a school or department nobody has posted before is still accepted with one click.

updates.title: One spelling per university, school and department
updates.summary: The same department used to appear several times over, because postings spelled it differently — Tulane's was listed as “Freeman School of Business, Management Science”, “Freeman School of Business, Management Sciences Area” and “A.B. Freeman School of Business, Management Science Department”, among others, so five postings of one department read as five different places. Every posting now names its university, school and department the one way — the school's full official name, and the department without the “Department”, “Area” or “group” each school words differently — across the current postings and the whole past-markets archive. Older archive entries that packed the university, school and department into a single line have been split into the three, so they now merge with the postings from the same place. New postings are tidied the same way as they arrive, and the posting form offers the spelling the site already uses.

updates.title: A new Operations Academia — one page, light or dark
updates.summary: The site has been redesigned. Everything for the market under way now reads as one scrolling page — job postings, candidates, placements, the survey, resources, the FAQ — with a flat keyword bar at the top instead of menus, and a light or dark mode you choose and the site remembers. The full filterable job list has its own page, as does the Universities map, the recent-faculty list and the past-markets archive, all rebuilt in the new look. Nothing moved address: every link you have saved still works, and the 2014–2026 site is still at /v1/.

updates.title: One spelling per country, everywhere on the site
updates.summary: The same country used to appear several times in the Location filter, because postings and the imported archive spelled it differently — “USA”, “UK”, “Hong Kong SAR”, “The Netherlands”, “Shenzhen, China”. Filtering on the United Kingdom therefore showed only a quarter of the British postings. Every country is now published under one full name (“United States”, “United Kingdom”), across the current postings and the whole past-markets archive, and new postings are tidied the same way as they arrive. Links you had already saved, and e-mail alerts you set up under the old spelling, keep working unchanged.

updates.title: Posting is simpler: every country listed, and no more “job market year” to work out
updates.summary: The country box on the job form now offers every country in the world, not just the three dozen that had posted before — and you can still type one that is not listed. The “Job market year” question is gone from the job and candidate forms: the site works the season out from the date and simply tells you which one your posting lands in. (Reporting a placement still asks, because an offer accepted in the spring and reported in the autumn belongs to the market it was accepted in.) Correcting an older posting now also keeps it in its own season instead of quietly moving it to the current one.

updates.title: A job posting now stays listed until its deadline passes
updates.summary: Job postings used to disappear from the list when the job market year rolled over on 1 July, even when applications were still open — an advert posted in May with a September deadline vanished in July. Now a posting stays on the job postings page for as long as its closing date has not passed, whichever season it was filed in. Postings with no fixed deadline (“until filled”) still move to the past-markets archive when the new market year begins.

updates.title: Merging two accounts now moves every posting you own
updates.summary: If you ended up with two accounts — say Google once and ORCID another time — merging them now hands over your candidate profile and your placement reports along with your job postings, so nothing is left behind on the account that is removed. Also fixed: posting a job with the advert file attached (rather than linked) was refused by a too-tight database bound; attached files now go through.

updates.title: The Universities map, Past job postings and Recent faculty now run on the site itself
updates.summary: The last three vendor tables are gone: the Universities page is now the site's own interactive map (search, clustered pins, and per-school links into candidates, jobs and placements), Past job postings is a filterable archive of every recorded market — including seasons that were previously nowhere on the site — and Recent faculty keeps its familiar list with shareable filtered links. Every deep link that worked before still works.

updates.title: The new site is live — and the old one is archived at /v1
updates.summary: The rebuilt site now IS operationsacademia.org: every page, the job postings list, posting a job, e-mail alerts and feedback all run on the site's own machinery, with no third-party table service in the reading path. The previous version is preserved exactly as it was at operationsacademia.org/v1, for reference.

updates.title: The job postings page shows the market year under way
updates.summary: The list now carries exactly the season its title names: postings filed since 1 July, plus anything a school has already advertised for this market or the next. Previous seasons remain in the archive at /v1 and in the site's records.

updates.title: Candidate profiles are posted on the site itself
updates.summary: Job-market candidates now create their profile directly on the site: sign in once, fill in the form, upload a CV and a research summary, and the profile appears on the Candidates page at the next update. Because the profile is tied to your account, you can come back to correct it, replace or remove your files, or take the profile down — none of which was possible before.

updates.title: Confirmed placements are reported on the site itself
updates.summary: Reporting a confirmed placement is now a form on the site: who, from which PhD program, joining which institution as what. The placement appears on the Placements page at the next update, and the person who reported it can correct or withdraw it.

updates.title: A What's-new page, with e-mail updates you can subscribe to
updates.summary: About → What's new lists every change to the site, newest first — this page you are reading. It is generated from the same record the e-mail digests are sent from, so signing in and subscribing to site updates delivers exactly these entries to your inbox as they ship.

updates.title: Every page of the site is now in the new version
updates.summary: The new site used to hold only the rebuilt pages — job postings, posting a job, e-mail alerts and feedback — while everything else still pointed at the old one. Every remaining page has now been carried across, identical in content and look, so the whole site can be browsed in the new version from home page to footer without ever leaving it.

updates.title: A site-wide review, and dozens of fixes
updates.summary: The whole of the new site was reviewed page by page and script by script. Among the fixes: the header's Feedback button no longer covers the navigation menu on smaller laptops; on a phone, signing in and out now works from the menu panel; searching inside a filter box types correctly; printed pages include each posting's details; filters can be combined without the menu closing after every tick; and e-mail alerts are delivered exactly once per posting.

updates.title: Signed up twice? Merge the two accounts into one
updates.summary: You can sign in with Google, with ORCID, or with an e-mail address and a password — and until now each of those started a separate account, because ORCID shares no e-mail address for us to recognise you by. So did a second Gmail address. Two accounts meant your alerts on one and your job postings on the other. Edit profile now offers 'Merge this account into another of mine': you sign in to the one you want to keep, and everything moves across — your alerts with their history intact, your job postings still yours to correct or withdraw, and any details the account you keep was missing. Nothing is deleted until the move has succeeded. The same card also lets you attach a second sign-in to the account you already have, so it never happens again — and if we spot that an ORCID registration duplicates an account you already had, we say so and offer the merge instead of leaving you to find it.

updates.title: The job filters read as they always did, and the list feels it
updates.summary: The Deadline filter offers exactly the three choices the old table did — Closing soon, Expired and Until filled — so a posting whose closing date is still ahead is described the way it has always been described. A value you have chosen can now be removed by clicking anywhere on its blue tag, rather than having to hit the small × on it. And the posting under your pointer now lifts gently off the page, so it is obvious which one you are about to open.

updates.title: A proper account menu, and a profile with your name on it
updates.summary: Signed-in visitors now get an account button in the header carrying their initials and their name, opening a menu with everything their account can do: post a job, e-mail alerts, edit profile, send feedback, sign out. A new profile card lets you set the name you are known by — until now the site could only greet you by half of your e-mail address. Posting a job also asks you to sign in or register up front, rather than after the form has been filled in.

updates.title: Every job posting is listed again
updates.summary: Postings submitted through the old form kept arriving after the new list was built from a one-off copy of the spreadsheet, so the new page had fallen behind the old one. The spreadsheet is now read automatically twice an hour and anything missing is added, so both lists show the same postings until the old form is retired.

updates.title: The job postings list is now our own
updates.summary: The job postings page no longer depends on a third-party table service. It is built from data held in the site's own repository, so it loads faster, keeps working if any vendor goes away, and can be improved whenever we like. Filtering behaves as before, with one addition: a filtered view now has its own web address, so you can bookmark or share exactly what you are looking at.

updates.title: Posting a job no longer goes through a third-party form
updates.summary: Job postings are submitted on the site itself. You sign in once, and your posting appears on the list automatically, normally within the hour. Because it is tied to your account, you can come back to correct a deadline or a broken link, or withdraw the posting once the search closes — none of which was possible before.

updates.title: Accounts, and e-mail alerts you control
updates.summary: You can now create a free account and subscribe to e-mail alerts: every new job posting, or only the ones matching filters you choose — a country, a rank, a type of school. You pick how often to hear from us, and every message carries a one-click unsubscribe.

updates.title: A feedback page that actually closes the loop
updates.summary: Report a problem, attach a screenshot, and get a ticket number — no account needed. When the thing you reported is fixed, you get an e-mail telling you what was done and linking to it.
